title: Desk damaged credit note: an omitted saleable follows the reason (false for return_damaged) and saleable:true with return_damaged is refused (400 return_not_saleable)
rootCause:
CONFIRMED (re-traced 2026-09-13). One cause, reachable only by a direct API call.

1. Contract. backend/libs/contracts/src/billing.ts:601: `saleable: z.boolean().default(true)` in CreditNoteLineInput (:597-603). Zod writes `true` into an omitted flag before the handler runs, whatever `reason` is (CreateCreditNoteInput.reason, :613). The service cannot tell "left out" from "saleable".

2. Service. backend/libs/core/src/modules/billing/credit-notes.service.ts: `create()` (:159-170) hands the parsed input to `draft()` (:263-387). draft returns an existing note with the same id first (:288), then checks each line:
   - the line belongs to the bill (:311-314)
   - pieces left to credit (:315-320)
   - the rate ceiling (:323-328)
   It never compares `line.saleable` with `input.reason`, and stores `saleable: line.saleable` (:347). The note and line inserts come after the loop (:357-385).

3. Stock. `issueInTx()` (:393-452) calls `restock()` (:459-495). `RESTOCKING_REASONS` includes 'return_damaged' (:98-103). The location then depends only on the line flag: `line.saleable ? saleableLocation : damagedLocation` (:484), ledger reason `sale_return_saleable` (:486-488). saleableLocation is the order's fulfil-from location, else the first active warehouse (`defaultRestockLocation` :497-508, `locationOfKind` :514-529). Result: return_damaged with a defaulted line posts sale_return_saleable into the Godown.

4. Same default on the other entry. `raiseForDelivery()` does `saleable: l.saleable ?? true` (:149). The doorstep is safe only because DOS-058 refuses the contradiction first (delivery/deliveries.service.ts:347-351). It picks 'return_damaged' only when every returned line is unsaleable (:187-191) and always passes an explicit boolean (:204).

5. Why DOS-058's predicate cannot be called as is. `isSaleableReturn` (contracts/src/delivery.ts:194-203) takes a DeliveryLineReason ('damaged', 'expired'), not a credit-note reason. There is no 'return_expired' in CreditNoteReasonSchema (contracts/src/billing.ts:107-115) or in the pg enum credit_note_reason (database/src/schema/billing.ts:200).

6. Harm downstream. claims/build.service.ts:468-481 counts every 'return_damaged' credit-note line as a brand damage-claim candidate, whatever its `saleable`. Such a note puts the pieces back on sale AND claims them from the brand.

7. No second cause (checked):
   - Offline: billing's sync tables are pull-only (`writable: false`, billing.module.ts:25-35), so no /sync/upload op creates a credit note. The doorstep op goes through deliveries.record and DOS-058 (delivery.sync.ts:132).
   - Worker: nothing in backend/worker/src writes credit notes (git grep: no match).
   - Writers of credit_note_lines: only draft() (:385) and the seed. seed-demo/billing.ts:1218 writes `saleable: spec.restock` (:1135); seed-demo/sales.ts:3025 writes `saleable: restock?.reason === 'sale_return_saleable'` (:2025). Every seeded return_damaged line in dos_qa is unsaleable.
   - Database: the service never relies on the column default `saleable ... default(true)` (schema/billing.ts:278). No trigger or RLS policy reads the flag.

8. The screens are already right:
   - frontend/manager-app/app/billing/credit-notes.tsx:168 sends `saleable: input.reason !== 'return_damaged'` (web regression 'wrong-day-4b' PASS). The screen has no per-line saleable control.
   - frontend/owner-app/app/billing/credit-notes.tsx only issues (:63) and cancels.
   - No other app calls creditNotes.create (git grep frontend).

9. Data (dos_qa, read-only, 2026-09-13):
   - 16 issued return_damaged notes. Exactly one has a saleable line: CN/9005 (desk, no delivery_id), the finding's own probe.
   - The other 15 are unsaleable: 12 from the desk, including the control CN/9006, and 3 from the doorstep (CN/9004, CN/9007, CN/9008).
   - 0 draft notes of any reason.
   - This matches reconcile check 09c(i).

changes.what:
CreditNoteLineInput (:591-603): change `saleable: z.boolean().default(true)` to `saleable: z.boolean().optional()`.

Add a field doc comment:
- When omitted, the flag follows the note's reason: false for `return_damaged` (its pieces go to the damaged bin), true for every other reason.
- A `return_damaged` line with `saleable: true` is refused with 400 `return_not_saleable`. This is the doorstep rule (DOS-058).

Add one sentence to the CreateCreditNoteInput doc (:605-609): damaged or expired goods returned at the desk are booked as `return_damaged`.

No new export and no enum change. CreditNoteLineSchema, the output shape (:302-303), is unchanged.

(a) After RESTOCKING_REASONS (:97-103), add `const UNSALEABLE_REASONS = new Set<CreditNoteReason>(['return_damaged'])`. Comment it as the credit-note side of UNSALEABLE_RETURN_REASONS (contracts/src/delivery.ts:194, DOS-058).

(b) raiseForDelivery (:149): change `saleable: l.saleable ?? true` to `saleable: l.saleable`, so draft() is the one place the default is decided.
- Delivery always passes a boolean (deliveries.service.ts:204), so the doorstep is unchanged.
- Update the `saleable?` doc in RaiseForDeliveryInput (:115): when omitted, it follows the reason.

(c) draft() line type (:277): change `saleable: boolean` to `saleable?: boolean | undefined`. This is required: backend/libs/config/tsconfig/base.json:8 turns on exactOptionalPropertyTypes, and CreateIn's lines now carry an optional key.

(d) In draft()'s line loop, right after the rate-ceiling check (:324-328) and before `values.push`:
- `const unsaleable = UNSALEABLE_REASONS.has(input.reason)`
- `const saleable = line.saleable ?? !unsaleable`
- `if (saleable && unsaleable) throw new ORPCError('BAD_REQUEST', { message, data: { code: 'return_not_saleable', invoiceLineId: source.id, reason: input.reason } })`
- message is the template literal '<source.description>: damaged goods go to the damaged bin, not back on sale'.

At :347, store `saleable` instead of `line.saleable`.

Why nothing is written on a refusal: the throw happens inside withTenant + idempotent, before the note insert (:357) and the line insert (:385). The transaction rolls back, and the idempotency row goes with it. The early replay return (:288) stays first. restock(), issueInTx() and issue() are unchanged.

(e) Add one line to the draft() doc comment (:257-262): when a line omits the flag, its disposition follows the reason, and a damaged return is never saleable.

Add three tests right after 'sends a damaged return to the damaged bin and moves nothing for a financial note' (ends :903), before the 'the other two sources of a bill' divider. Existing tests stay unchanged.

FIXTURE
- Each test gets its own fresh bill: `placeOrder(rep, shopMh, [{ variantId: variantA, cases: 1 }], tag)`, then `issueFor(orderId, tag)` (12 pcs).
- There is enough stock: beforeAll posts 5 000 opening pcs of variantA to the godown (:427-455), and shopMh has no credit limit. So there is no fallback to creditedInvoiceId, and separate bills keep the pieces-left counts independent.
- Tags are 'dos116-omit', 'dos116-refuse' and 'dos116-guard'. DOS-126's spec uses 'dos126', so the keys cannot collide.
- Credit notes are posted as `manager` (a CREDIT_NOTE_RAISER), not `driver`, so nothing here depends on DOS-115.
- The tenant has exactly one warehouse ('Godown', tenant-bootstrap.ts:195) and one damaged bin, so the default restock location is `godown`.
- Type the error body `{ message?: string; data?: { code?: string; invoiceLineId?: string; reason?: string } }`, as in delivery.spec.ts:885-887.

TEST 1 (red)
(a) POST /credit-notes { reason: 'return_damaged', autoIssue: true, lines: [{ id, invoiceLineId, qtyPcs: 2 }] }, saleable omitted.
   - Expect 200, item.state 'issued', item.lines[0].saleable false.
   - ledgerFor(noteId) is exactly one row { reason: 'sale_return_damaged', qty_delta: 2, location_id: damaged }.
(b) The desk's two-step flow on the same bill: POST /credit-notes with autoIssue omitted, qtyPcs 2, saleable omitted.
   - Expect 200, state 'draft', lines[0].saleable false, and ledgerFor empty.
   - Then POST /credit-notes/{id}/issue: expect 200 and exactly one ledger row, sale_return_damaged +2 at damaged.

TEST 2 (red)
For autoIssue in [true, false], with a fresh id and key `cn-dos116-refuse-${String(autoIssue)}-${run}`:
- POST /credit-notes { reason: 'return_damaged', autoIssue, lines: [{ id, invoiceLineId, qtyPcs: 2, saleable: true }] }.
- Expect 400: body.data.code 'return_not_saleable', data.invoiceLineId is the bill line, data.reason 'return_damaged', and the message matches /damaged bin/.
- SQL: no credit_notes row with that id, no credit_note_lines row with that credit_note_id, and ledgerFor(id) empty.
- Resend the SAME key and id with saleable: false: expect 200. This proves the refusal left no idempotency row behind.

TEST 3 (guard: passes before and after, and is named as a guard)
- POST /credit-notes { reason: 'return_saleable', autoIssue: true, lines: [{ id, invoiceLineId, qtyPcs: 1 }] }, saleable omitted.
- Expect 200, lines[0].saleable true, and exactly one ledger row { reason: 'sale_return_saleable', qty_delta: 1, location_id: godown }.
- It proves that moving the default out of Zod changes nothing for the other reasons.

contractChange:
backend/libs/contracts/src/billing.ts, CreditNoteLineInput.saleable: `z.boolean().default(true)` becomes `z.boolean().optional()`, plus a doc comment stating the rule.

Why it is needed: with the Zod default, the server cannot tell an omitted flag from an explicit `true`. The founder's rule (docs/22:277) needs an omitted flag to follow the reason.

Why it breaks nothing:
- Every request that parsed before still parses. The procedure, path, method and permissions are unchanged.
- The client-side input type (z.input) is `saleable?: boolean | undefined` before and after, so the frontend sees no type change.
- The parsed type (z.output) becomes optional. Its only consumer is CreditNotesService (CreateIn, credit-notes.service.ts:72), handled by change (c).
- CreditNoteLineSchema.saleable, the output, is unchanged.
- The generated READMEs should not change. The sampler renders `true` for a defaulted boolean and for an optional one alike (core/src/docs/sample.ts:171-174, :185-188, :203-204), and the request-body table lists only top-level fields (:218-231).
- Only the runtime /docs/openapi.json loses `default: true` on lines[].saleable, and no OpenAPI file is checked in.
migration:
none.
- credit_note_lines.saleable keeps its column default (schema/billing.ts:278), and the service always writes an explicit value.
- No database-level check is added. The reason lives on credit_notes and the flag on credit_note_lines, so such a check would need a trigger and a 0045 migration. The architect design does not ask for one.
decisionsNeeded:
none. The founder's rule is already in docs/22-source-of-truth.md:277 (§8) and in the change log at :334.

Not blocking: expired goods returned at the desk will print as 'Goods returned (damaged)'. If the founder wants them to print as 'expired', that needs a new credit-note reason (enum migration, contract, PDF label, claims) and is a separate item.
architectDesignFollowed:
amended in four points, each forced by the code:

1. No `return_expired`.
- The design names `return_expired`, but no such reason exists in CreditNoteReasonSchema (contracts/src/billing.ts:107-115) or in the pg enum credit_note_reason (database/src/schema/billing.ts:200).
- The rule therefore covers `return_damaged`, the only credit-note reason for unsaleable goods. Expired stock returned at the desk is booked as return_damaged, which satisfies docs/22:277 ("damaged or expired goods").
- Adding a reason needs an enum migration, a contract change, app strings and PDF labels. That is outside this finding.

2. The contract default has to go.
- "Lines default to saleable:false" cannot work while the contract says `.default(true)`, because Zod fills in `true` before the handler runs.
- The field becomes `.optional()`, and the service works out the default from the reason.

3. The rule sits in CreditNotesService.draft(), not in create() alone.
- Both paths go through draft(): `billing.creditNotes.create` (owner :3001, manager and accountant :3002, delivery :3005) and the in-process `raiseForDelivery`.
- raiseForDelivery's own `?? true` is removed, so there is one rule in one place.

4. DOS-058's `isSaleableReturn` is not called.
- It takes a delivery reason and cannot accept 'return_damaged'.
- What is reused is its error contract: BAD_REQUEST with data { code: 'return_not_saleable', invoiceLineId, reason } and a message naming the damaged bin. A billing-local UNSALEABLE_REASONS sits next to RESTOCKING_REASONS.
- A shared predicate in contracts, the DOS-058 file pattern, was considered and not adopted. The manager screen already sends the right flag, and moving it to a shared predicate would pull a frontend change and an Android/iOS re-walk into a server fix.

WHAT CHANGES
Only reason return_damaged is affected:
- An omitted saleable now means unsaleable (it meant saleable).
- An explicit saleable:true now returns 400 (it returned 200).

Every other reason still defaults to true, and the guard test pins that. return_saleable with unsaleable lines stays allowed; the doorstep raises mixed returns that way (deliveries.service.ts:187-205).

CALLERS CHECKED
- The manager screen already sends false for return_damaged (credit-notes.tsx:168). The owner app only issues and cancels, and no other app creates notes.
- Smoke pins short_delivery (smoke-endpoints.mts:1553-1566), and the README example samples short_delivery.
- Delivery raises return_damaged only with all-false lines.
- Seed-demo inserts issued notes directly, with saleable worked out from the restock (seed-demo/sales.ts:2025, seed-demo/billing.ts:1135). It does not go through the service.
- No spec or QA tool sends return_damaged with saleable omitted or true. git grep finds only billing.spec.ts:871, with false, and delivery.spec.ts.

IDEMPOTENCY EDGE
- The request hash is the JSON of the parsed input (platform/idempotency.ts:55). An omitted flag used to hash as true; now it is absent.
- A client that retries a pre-fix key across the restart with the flag omitted gets 409 instead of the stored reply.
- The manager app always sends the flag, so its hashes do not change, and nothing is deployed yet.

DRAFTS ARE NOT RE-CHECKED AT ISSUE
- The architect design scopes the rule to create.
- A return_damaged draft with a saleable line written before the fix would still restock the godown when issued.
- dos_qa has 0 drafts of any reason, the seed writes only issued notes, and verify step 0 checks again before the running-product pass.

CN/9005
It is an issued, immutable document with an append-only ledger row. It is not repaired, and it disappears with the Q5 rebuild of dos_qa.
